INTER AGENCY AGREEMENT BETWEEN
STATE OF WYOMING, DEPARTMENT OF STATE PARKS AND CULTURAL
RESOURCES, DIVISION OF STATE PARKS, HISTORIC SITES&TRAILS
AND CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING
1.
Parties.The parties to this Inter agency Agreement(Agreement) are the State of Wyoming,
Department of State Parks and Cultural Resources, Division of State Parks, Historic Sites
&Trails (State Parks), whose address is: 2301 Central Avenue, Cheyenne, WY 82002, and
the City of Cheyenne (City), whose address is:2101 O'Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY
82001.
2.
Purpose of Agreement.The purpose of this Agreement is to outline projects,
responsibilities, and special provisions at the High Plains Research Station and Arboretum
(Site), including the following:
1.Roles and responsibilities of State Parks;
2.Roles and responsibilities of the City, including the Community Recreation and
Events Department, Divisions of Cheyenne Urban Forestry and the Cheyenne
Botanic Gardens; and
Wyoming State Legislature.
3.
Term of Agreement.This Agreement is effective when all parties have executed it
(Effective Date). The term of this Agreement is from the Effective Date through June 30,
2026.There is no right or expectation of extension and any extension will be determined
at the discretion of State Parks.
4.
Agreement.

The State Parks Representative or their designee shall be responsible for
corresponding and arranging meetings with City personnel and outside Agencies

7.
Special Provisions.
A.
State Parks and the City shall develop along-term lease for the property, which will
go into effect should legislation pass designating the Site as a State Historic Site.
Such a lease will detail the legal description of the site, terms and conditions for
use and management of the site, length of the lease, termination clauses, external
partnerships, and other general provisions.
B.
Uponpassage of legislation designating the Site as a State Historic Site, the City
shall introduce, through City Council, a measure to amend thelong-term lease of
the Sitewith the United States Department of Agriculture-Agricultural Research
Service (USDA-ARS). This request shall include the return of sections of property
identified by the survey as well as buildings identified by the USDA.Such a
request would need to be referred to committee, and pass the voting process, and
will reference the formal land survey and the transfer of several historic buildings.
C.
Upon passage of a lease modification referenced above in Section 7.B, the City
shall approach USDA-ARS with the proposed lease modifications, beginning the
process to return land and assets to the Cityfor inclusion into along-term lease with
State Parks.
